passages.note: Bill overview lists Kavanagh as a co-sponsor of the AZ ESA expansion bill.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: New ARS 15-2401.01 makes any public-school-eligible resident a qualified student for an ESA, i.e. universal eligibility; existing 'qualified school' definition (nongovernmental, non-discriminatory) does not exclude religious schools.
House Third Reading: Kavanagh voted Y on final passage, 31-26-3-0-0 (not near-unanimous).

rows.reasoning: As a State Representative, Kavanagh co-sponsored and voted Yea on HB 2853 (2022), which added ARS 15-2401.01 making any resident eligible to enroll in a public preschool-for-disabilities, kindergarten, or grades 1-12 program a 'qualified student' for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account, and whose existing 'qualified school' definition (nongovernmental, non-discriminatory) does not exclude religious schools. This matches rung 5, "universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious." Per the V5 earlier-chamber ruling, his House-era record counts as in-term for his current Senate seat.
